items.title: Every vacancy has a price
items.body:
Every vacancy has a price. Most businesses never work it out.

Not because they do not care. Because nobody sat down and did the sum: the salary budget that is not producing work, the colleagues covering the gap, the customers who wait a little longer.

If you are planning to hire in 2027, start with the number.

items.title: Does your offer stand out?
items.body:
A good candidate rarely has just one option.

By the time your offer lands, they may already be talking to two other employers. So the question is not "is our offer fair?" It is "does it stand out?"

What tends to separate strong offers from forgettable ones:

▪ A clear salary, not "competitive"
▪ A fast, honest process with a named person to contact
▪ A role that matches the advert
▪ Something concrete about the first 90 days

The Offer Strength step in our free Hiring Toolkit shows where your offer is likely to win a good candidate and where it may lose them.

👉 {link}

#Recruitment #Hiring #EmployerBrand #UKJobs

items.title: The one change to most job adverts
items.body:
If I could change one thing about most job adverts, it would be this: say what the job pays.

Not "competitive". The actual range. Good candidates skip adverts that make them guess.

Then say what the process is and who they will meet. That alone puts you ahead of most employers.

If you want a quick read on how strong your offer looks to a candidate, the free Hiring Toolkit has a step for exactly that.

#Hiring #JobAdverts #Recruitment

items.title: Slow hiring loses good people
items.body:
Slow hiring does not look slow from the inside. It looks careful.

From the candidate's side it looks different. Five signs your process may be losing people:

1. Applicants wait more than a few days to hear anything
2. There are three or four interview rounds for a mid-level role
3. The salary is only revealed late
4. Nobody owns the process, so nobody replies
5. The role described at interview is not the role advertised

None of this is about effort. It is about gaps nobody has looked at.

Our free Hiring Health Score looks at them for you, in a few minutes.

👉 {link}

#Hiring #Recruitment #CandidateExperience #SmallBusiness

items.title: Why good candidates drop out
items.body:
Good candidates rarely withdraw because of one big thing. It is usually a few small ones: nobody replied, the process dragged, the role was not quite what the advert said.

All of it is fixable, and most of it costs nothing.

If you want to see where your own process might be leaking people, the Hiring Health Score in our free toolkit is a good place to start.

items.title: READ FIRST: cold email and LinkedIn rules
items.body:
WHO TO EMAIL
▪ Named hiring contacts at limited companies and LLPs (check Companies House if unsure)
▪ Skip sole traders, ordinary partnerships and personal email addresses (Gmail, Hotmail and so on). They are treated like consumers, so cold email needs their consent
▪ Skip anyone on the Suppression List, and check the email status in the Lead Pipeline before sending

HOW TO SEND
▪ One to one, personalised, from Outlook. On the Review and Send panel use "Download .eml instead", so first-touch cold email stays off Brevo and its sender reputation is protected
▪ Roughly 15 to 20 new first-touch emails a day, and 20 to 25 LinkedIn connection requests a day

EVERY EMAIL MUST
▪ Say who you are and why you are writing
▪ Say how you found them (company website, LinkedIn, their advert)
▪ Be relevant to a role or need you can see
▪ End with a clear opt-out line, and one ask only

SEQUENCE
▪ Email 1 on day 0, Email 2 on day 4, Email 3 on day 9. Then stop for 90 days

OPT-OUTS
▪ If anyone says no, add them to the Suppression List the same day

THE BRIDGE TO BREVO
▪ If someone replies positively, ask "Would you like our quarterly Hiring Pulse?" Add them to Brevo only after a yes

NO FEES OR PRICES in any message. If they ask what we charge, use the Reply message.
items.notes: Internal guide for Ella and Dan. Not for sending.

Hi [First name],

A quick follow-up. Some employers find a young hire, trained their way, becomes one of the strongest people in the team. The hard part is finding the right person and understanding what support is available.

If you would like a short call, I will explain what we are building, and you can tell me whether it is useful.

If this is not relevant, just reply "no thanks" and I will not email you again.

Daniel Brown
Director, Live 2 Help Recruitment
items.notes: HOLD. Same conditions as Email 1.

items.title: Group Buyer - Venesta (Guy Saunders)
items.body:
Subject: Group Buyer - where we left it

Guy,

I have not wanted to chase after Mark P. You said you wanted someone different, and that was a fair call.

Here is what I have changed on the search. I am now screening specifically for a data-driven buyer who can hold their own with senior stakeholders, and I am preparing every candidate for scored competency interviews with specific commercial examples, which is what you look for.

[ONLY IF SCREENED: one line on the buyer with the JCB manufacturing background. Anonymised, no name.]

What is your take?

Daniel Brown
Director, Live 2 Help Recruitment
items.notes: Dan to CALL Guy first (no response since Mark P was rejected), then send this. Only include the buyer line once the screener is complete.

items.title: Regional Sales Manager - Ceasefire (Arnab Das)
items.body:
Subject: Regional Sales Manager - keeping it warm

Arnab,

No CV to push today. I am keeping the search open for the person who clears the bar you and Darren set: real fire industry credibility and an existing book of trade partners.

I will only send someone when they clear both. If the brief has moved since we last spoke, tell me and I will adjust.

What is your take?

Daniel Brown
Director, Live 2 Help Recruitment
items.notes: Ceasefire is passive. Check-in only, no speculative submission.

items.title: Dormant client email 1
items.body:
Subject: It has been a while, [First name]

Hi [First name],

It has been a while since we last spoke about hiring at [Company]. Are you planning to recruit this year?

If so, reply with one line about the role and I will tell you what I am seeing in the market for it.


Daniel Brown
Director, Live 2 Help Recruitment
items.notes: Day 0. Ask: one line on the role. For past clients, not cold prospects.

items.title: Dormant client email 2
items.body:
Subject: Re: It has been a while, [First name]

Hi [First name],

Following up in case this got buried. Hiring is moving again for a lot of employers, and I would rather speak to you before a role becomes urgent.

Fifteen minutes this week or next?


Daniel Brown
Director, Live 2 Help Recruitment
items.notes: Day 5. Ask: a 15 minute call.

items.title: Proof Engine routine
items.body:
EVERY 2 WEEKS
▪ Dan sends one fresh candidate review
▪ Remove every name (including Dan's), the company name and anything that identifies the person
▪ Paste it into the next Proof Engine review post, add the graphic, schedule for Thursday 08:00 on the company page and Ella's page

WHEN A ROLE IS FILLED
▪ Ask the client if they are happy for the win to be mentioned
▪ Post the placement template with the role title and sector only, no names

NEVER
▪ Name reviewers or clients without written permission
▪ Point people to Google to find the originals
▪ Mention fees or prices
items.notes: Internal guide. Not for sending.

items.title: How referrals work
items.body:
THE SPIRIT
▪ A natural two-way relationship. No fees, no contract, no outsourced business development
▪ Reciprocation is welcome but never expected

WHEN A PARTNER INTRODUCES SOMEONE
▪ Ask the partner to introduce us by email or in person. Do not take contact details without the person knowing
▪ Log the contact in the CRM with the source "Referral - [partner name]"
▪ Thank the partner personally, whatever happens next

WHEN WE INTRODUCE SOMEONE
▪ Ask the business owner first. Introduce only with their agreement
▪ Never promise an outcome on the partner's behalf

DATA
▪ Share only what the person has agreed to share
items.notes: Internal guide. Not for sending.

items.title: Connection note - referral partner
items.body: Hi [First name] - I run Live 2 Help Recruitment and often meet business owners who need help beyond hiring. Would be good to connect and see if we can help each other's clients.
items.notes: Under 300 characters.

items.title: First message - referral partner
items.body:
Thanks for connecting, [First name].

I work with owner-managed businesses on hiring, and I often meet people who need help with [their service]. If a client of yours ever asks "do you know a good recruiter?", I would be glad to be the name you give. And I will do the same for you.

No fees and no paperwork, just a natural exchange. Would a 20 minute call be useful?
items.notes: Keep the tone casual.

items.title: Email 1 - referral partner
items.body:
Subject: A natural fit, [First name]?

Hi [First name],

I am Daniel Brown, and I run Live 2 Help Recruitment. I found [Company] through [source], and I think we serve some of the same people.

Your clients are often at the stage where hiring is the next step. When they ask whether you know a good recruiter, I would like to be the name you give. And when I meet business owners who need [their service], I would be glad to point them to you.

No fees, no paperwork. Just a simple, honest exchange. Would a 20 minute call be worth it?

If this is not relevant, just reply "no thanks" and I will not email you again.

Daniel Brown
Director, Live 2 Help Recruitment
items.notes: Day 0. Ask: a 20 minute call. Reciprocal, no fees.

items.title: Email 2 - referral partner follow-up
items.body:
Subject: Re: A natural fit, [First name]?

Hi [First name],

A quick follow-up. If it helps your clients straight away, we have a free Hiring Toolkit that shows what an open role is costing a business and how strong their offer is: {link}

Feel free to pass it on. And if a call would be useful, say when.

If this is not relevant, just reply "no thanks" and I will not email you again.

Daniel Brown
Director, Live 2 Help Recruitment
items.notes: Day 5. Ask: share the toolkit or take a call.

items.title: Reply - invite to the Hiring Pulse
items.body:
Glad that was useful, [First name].

Once a quarter we send a short note on what we are seeing in live hiring: what is working, what is not and one thing worth changing. Would you like it in your inbox? Reply "yes" and I will add you. You can unsubscribe at any time.
items.notes: The bridge from cold outreach to Brevo. Add them to the Brevo Hiring Pulse list only after a yes, and record the date and source.

items.title: Brevo setup - lists and consent (do first)
items.next_step: Confirm which Brevo account to use, then create the Live 2 Help lists
items.notes:
The Brevo account is shared with The Stoic Architect (F5IVE lists). Live 2 Help has its own authenticated domain and senders (office@ and clients@).

Create three Live 2 Help lists: L2H Clients, L2H Opted-in Leads, L2H Talent Suite Candidates.

Consent attributes on each contact: CONSENT_SOURCE (Hiring Toolkit, Talent Suite, reply, client) and CONSENT_DATE.

Rules: no imports of scraped, purchased or third-party lists. Cold prospects stay out of Brevo until they say yes. Every email carries an unsubscribe link and the company name and address.

Free plan note: the free plan has a daily send limit, so large sends are staged.

items.title: Hiring Pulse - quarterly newsletter
items.audience: L2H Opted-in Leads and L2H Clients
items.next_step: Build the navy and gold template, then the January issue as a draft
items.notes:
Issue outline (about 250 words):
1. One headline insight from live hiring
2. One practical tip
3. One thing to try: the free Hiring Toolkit
4. Sign-off from Dan and Ella

Send quarterly: January and April. Always a draft first, test email to Dan and Ella, then send.

items.title: Hiring Toolkit follow-up
items.audience: Toolkit completions with the consent box ticked
items.next_step: Build after the Brevo lists exist
items.notes:
Email 1 (same day): a recap of their results and an offer to talk through them.
Email 2 (day 3): one offer-strength tip.
Email 3 (day 10): a gentle check-in on the role they were thinking about.

Only for people who ticked the consent box. Others get a personal email from Ella only.

items.title: Talent Suite New Year nurture
items.audience: Talent Suite sign-ups who opted in to marketing
items.next_step: Check the sign-up form has a separate marketing consent box first
items.notes:
Email 1 (day 1): welcome and the three best first steps in the toolkit.
Email 2 (day 7): Job Match Score tip.
Email 3 (day 14): the 1-to-1 recruiter sessions, no prices in the email.

If the sign-up form does not have its own marketing consent box, only service emails can be sent until it does.
